claim: V02 §5.7 (4), §2.4's `ExteriorDamage.look.kind` comment and X35 take the disaster's kind from 'the calamity's type V01's `disasterDistricts` reads for its pattern'. But `disasterDistricts` returns only `Id[]` (V01 §2.3; R2-37 (4)). The calamity and its pattern are `disasterSource(doc, overlay, key)`'s `calamity` and `pattern` (V01 §2.3, whose comments name V02 §5.7 (4) as their reader), and V02 §1b's input cell does not name `disasterSource`. A raw `type` word also leaves the fire flavour undefined for 'blaze', 'conflagration' or 'burning', which V06 §2.4's table reads as `fire` and V01's `pattern` already classifies.
required_change: V02 §5.7 (4) reads: "Its kind — V01's `disasterSource(doc, overlay, key).pattern` (V01 §2.3, V01 §3.16 (2): the calamity's type through V06 §2.4's calamity table; `scatter` for a preview) — adds one flavour: a `fire` pattern blackens, …; a `flood` and a `scatter` (an earthquake, every other kind, a preview) draw the damage alone". §2.4's `look.kind` becomes `pattern: 'fire'|'flood'|'scatter'` with the comment "V01's `DisasterSource.pattern`". V02 §1b's input cell and X35 name `disasterSource` beside `disasterDistricts`.

claim: `exteriorDamage(doc, b, view, opts)` (V02 §2.4) reads state that lives only in the generation worker: the document; V06's `decayLevel` and `decayPeak` over the lineage's lifecycle events; the plan in force from the elaboration cache (§2.8: the document's non-canonical blocks); V01's `disasterDistricts` and V06's `crisisLookYields`. Its consumer is 'V02 §5.7's drawing in the tile rasteriser' (V02 §1b). Its holes and gaps are 'memoised beside its roofscape' (V02 §5.7 (8), §6.6), which the tile worker derives from the display list (V02 §3.1's roofscape row; V02 §6.3); the tile worker holds no document, cache or lifecycle block. V02 names no path by which a building's damage reaches the tile worker (no mark, column or `DisplayDelta` group). Nor does it say when the damage is sent again: the drawn week crossing an element's threshold or a look's week edge, `crises` or the effective key changing, a plan coming into force (a click, `elaborate: 'view'`) or leaving it (eviction), a restoration. §8.1 item 7 re-emits only Works targets' marks on a week change. Producer and consumer sit in two workers with no wire between them.
required_change: V02 §5.7 (8) and §2.4 state four things. (1) `exteriorDamage` runs in the generation worker, where its inputs live, over the buildings of the tiles the view requests. (2) Its result reaches the tile worker as the building's damage marks — `level`, `reading`, the hole and patched rings, the gap spans, and the look's tone, dash and fire flags — in the building's group of a `DisplayDelta` (§8.1, §8.9). (3) It is re-emitted for exactly the buildings whose `ExteriorDamage` changes: when the drawn week moves (beside §8.1 item 7's Works re-emission), when `crises` or the effective knowledge key changes, when a plan enters or leaves force, and after a commit that moves a level or a look's units. (4) The tile worker clips the marks against the roofscape it memoises (V02 §6.3), the tile keyed as VV12-r2-06 states. V02 §1b's row names this path. V02 §6.6 adds the generation-worker cost per changed building. T-V2-59 (e) and T-V2-60 (g) add an eviction of the plan in force and a `crises` toggle, the tile redrawn after each.
